title: Inquest into Rodney Jackson's death reveals timeline of shooting
article: A timeline into the death of Rodney Shane Jackson in Terrace two years ago has emerged during the inquest in Terrace, and it shows just how quickly the fatal shooting happened.

On Thursday a neighbor of Jackson testified that he was always kind to her - picking berries, and chopping her wood. Asked if the RCMP ever came to Kisgegas to ask anyone about Jackson in the months leading up to the shooting - she said never - then one day a swat team arrives.

"You know here they are, camouflaged, armed, trained, and still had to shoot him," said Audrey Lundquist with a confused look on her face. "I don't understand it," she added, saying that she knows the Emergency Response Team is a "necessary evil" but there has to be some checks and balances in how they do things.

"Well I can't speak to the specifics of the circumstances that are being examined by the coroner's inquest however I can say that comprehensive threat-risk assessment is conducted along with operational planning, and contingencies are put in place before a determination is made to activate and deploy an emergency response team," said Rod Booth, RCMP's North District Superintendent,
On September 26 at about 7:55 a.m. an unmarked vehicle drops off seven ERT members about a kilometer from a cabin where Rodney Jackson was believed to be.

They split into Team A on one side of the road and Team B on the other. In camouflage they quietly advance through thick bush towards the cabin. But they are upwind and Jackson's two dogs catch their scent and start barking and running toward the team on the north side of the road.

Soon after - Rodney and his brother Robert come out of the cabin with loaded 303 rifles - perhaps thinking there was another bear around. They had already shot one and its carcass was hanging from a nearby tree.

Team B first spots Rodney walking quickly down the road toward them. At least two of the officers testified that they stood up in clear sight and yelled "police - drop your gun". Robert started to do just that but Rodney started to run north until he reached a steep ravine.
Here he stopped, and started to turn towards Team A still hiding in the bushes.
One of the officers on Team A had a good view of him and testified that he believed Rodney was turning to shoot him - even though Rodney had his rifle held in only one hand.
Then eight shots rang out in rapid fire - from one member of Team B; one of those bullets striking Rodney in the back.

The officer just five-feet behind the shooter testified that he did not see anything in Rodney's hand as the first shot was fired. From the time "police" drop your gun was heard - to the time Rodney was lying face down on the ground was estimated by one officer to be just three to four seconds.
